real_conflicts: The typography critic's proposal to reduce text opacity to 80% and allow the waveform to 'punch through' the letters is a direct threat to the production-level finish. It introduces visual muddiness that undermines the crisp, high-contrast identity of the poster and risks making the primary title difficult to read, which is a failure of craft.
accepted: The visual concept critic's suggestion to integrate the red diagonal line as a 'spike' in the waveform is accepted. This improves the graphical consistency by unifying the two main graphical elements into a single, cohesive system rather than disjointed overlays.
concession: I concede that the current 'neon glow' is too generic and lacks the specific atmospheric quality of a 'late-night' venue. It needs to be less 'digital sign' and more 'physical light in a dark room.'
compromise: Instead of the opacity reduction proposed by the typography critic, we will apply a subtle, high-frequency grain texture to the entire canvas. This will break up the sterile digital smoothness, add a tactile 'analog' feel that suits the 'experimental' brief, and allow the waveform to visually interact with the text through texture rather than transparency, preserving the sharpness of the type.
nonnegotiable: The high-contrast duotone palette of electric blue and signal red against a deep, near-black background is the core identity of the poster and must remain the dominant visual driver.
